'''King Kuok "Mimi" Hii''' (born 23 December 1969) is a chemist whose fields of research include application of catalysis to organic synthesis. She is the Director of [[Imperial College London]]'s Centre for Rapid Online Analysis of Reactions (ROAR).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imperial.ac.uk/a-z-research/rapid-online-analysis-of-reactions/|title=Centre for Rapid Online Analysis of Reactions (ROAR)|website=Imperial College London|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Hii studied for both her BSc and PhD at The [[University of Leeds]] investigating multidentate ligand metal complexes under the supervision of [[Bernard L. Shaw]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shaw|first1=Bernard L.|last2=Perera|first2=Sarath D.|last3=Hii|first3=King Kuok|date=1994-01-01|title=Terdentate (P–N–O) complexes formed from Z,E-PPh2CH2C-(But)N–NCH(C6H4OH-2) or Z,E-PPh2CH2C(But)N–NCH-[C6H2(OH-2)(OMe)2-4,6] and nickel, palladium, platinum, rhodium or iridium|journal=Journal of the Chemical Society, Dalton Transactions|issue=24|pages=3589–3596|doi=10.1039/DT9940003589|issn=1364-5447}}</ref>  Postdoctoral studies at [[University of Oxford|Oxford University]] in John M. Brown's group were followed by independent research at [[University of Leeds]], [[King's College London]] and in [[Imperial College London]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/tree.php?pid=93345|title=Chemistry Tree - King Kuok (Mimi) Hii Family Tree|website=academictree.org|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref> In 2016 she was awarded a Professorship in [[Catalysis]] and in 2018 became the Director of the Centre for Rapid Online Analysis of Reactions.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/190097/first-of-its-kind-automatic-chemistry-facility-opens-imperial/|title=First-of-its-kind automatic chemistry facility opens at Imperial {{!}} Imperial News {{!}} Imperial College London|website=Imperial News|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref>

== Research interests ==
Hii has investigated catalysis during her research career.  In Oxford, she characterised intermediates of the [[Heck reaction]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brown|first1=John M.|last2=Hii|first2=King Kuok (Mimi)|date=1996|title=Characterization of Reactive Intermediates in Palladium-Catalyzed Arylation of Methyl Acrylate (Heck Reaction)|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English|volume=35|issue=6|pages=657–659|doi=10.1002/anie.199606571|issn=1521-3773}}</ref> Hii also studied this reaction at King's College London.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Examination of Ligand Effects in the Heck Arylation Reaction|issue=40|pages=7975–7979|journal=Tetrahedron|volume=56|doi=10.1016/S0040-4020(00)00703-1|date=2000-09-29|last1=Qadir|first1=Maryiam|last2=Möchel|first2=Tobias|last3=(Mimi) Hii|first3=King Kuok}}</ref> Hii has continued with this field of study producing over a hundred articles, reviews, book chapters and patents. These include articles, reviews and books on sustainable chemistry methods.<ref>{{Cite book|date=2013-04-08|editor-last=Dunn|editor-first=Peter J.|editor2-last=Hii|editor2-first=K. K. Mimi|editor3-last=Krische|editor3-first=Michael J.|editor4-last=Williams|editor4-first=Michael T.|title=Sustainable Catalysis|doi=10.1002/9781118354520|isbn=9781118354520}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Leung|first1=Andrew Yuk Keung|last2=Hellgardt|first2=Klaus|last3=Hii|first3=King Kuok “Mimi”|date=2018-04-02|title=Catalysis in Flow: Nickel-Catalyzed Synthesis of Primary Amines from == Awards and honours ==
In 2013, the [[Federation of Asian Chemical Societies|Federation of Asian Chemistry Societies]] recognised Hii as an Asian Rising Star. Hii was also elected as a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Dr. King Kuok (Mimi) Hii |url=http://www.ch.ic.ac.uk/mimi/index_files/Page391.htm |accessdate=6 May 2019 |publisher=King Kuok Hii Lab, Imperial College London}}</ref> In 2016 Hii became co-editor in chief of the open access [[Chemistry Central Journal]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.springeropen.com/springeropen/2016/02/03/new-co-editor-chief-chemistry-central-journal/|title=New Co-Editor-in-Chief for Chemistry Central Journal|last=Hollingworth|first=Charlotte|date=2016-02-03|website=SpringerOpen blog|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref> In 2019 Mimi Hii was shortlisted for an Asian Women of Achievement Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.awaawards.com/our-alumni-category/2019/|title=2019|website=Asian Women of Achievement Awards|access-date=2019-05-06}}</ref>
